reviewers.summary: The changed resolver avoids counting unresolved module and variable principals as app grants, but now misses a real app grant when those references resolve to the app identity. That leaves RELEASE-ID-01 unenforced for this configuration.

findingList.message: The contract test can miss an app ACR grant routed through a Terraform variable or module output. Resolve those references or otherwise ensure an indirect grant to the app identity fails the RELEASE-ID-01 test.

evidence.codePathTraced: MayResolveToApp follows local references but skips var and module references. AppAcrGrantRoles therefore omits any ACR role assignment whose principal is supplied through a variable or module output.
evidence.failureScenario: If a child module assigns AcrPush to var.app_principal_id and its caller passes azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.principal_id, the contract test skips that grant. The assertion can still pass with only the expected AcrPull in its results, despite the app identity having an additional ACR grant.

reviewers.summary: The revised test avoids counting unresolved variable and module principals as app grants, but that also lets an extra ACR grant to the app identity evade the RELEASE-ID-01 contract check.

findingList.message: The contract test misses app ACR grants supplied through variables or module outputs. Resolve those references or make the test reject them when they could identify the app identity.

evidence.codePathTraced: MayGrantToApp calls MayResolveToApp, which follows local references but skips var and module references. An assignment using either reference is therefore omitted from AppAcrGrantRoles unless its expression also directly names the app identity.
evidence.failureScenario: If an additional AcrPush assignment has a direct ACR scope and its principal is var.app_principal_id or module.identity.principal_id resolving to the app identity, the contract test skips that grant and its exact-one AcrPull assertion still passes. This leaves the RELEASE-ID-01 least-privilege check bypassable (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

reviewers.summary: The latest change avoids counting unresolved module and variable principals as app grants, but this creates a bypass for a real app grant routed through a child module. The contract test can therefore pass despite an extra ACR grant to the app identity.

findingList.message: The contract test misses app ACR grants passed through module or variable principals. Resolve those references or ensure they fail the exact-one grant check.

evidence.codePathTraced: MayResolveToApp follows only local references. It skips var and module references, so MayGrantToApp excludes assignments whose principal reaches the app identity through a module input.
evidence.failureScenario: If a child module assigns AcrPush on the ACR using principal_id = var.principal_id and the root module passes azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.principal_id as that input, AppAcrGrantRoles skips the assignment. The contract test can pass with the extra app grant, contrary to AC RELEASE-ID-01 (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).
